title_en: Brahmaruli - hymn to the Supreme Brahman
translation:
[Here begins Shri Brahmaruli ||3||. Every verse carries the refrain "ture brahmaruli", shortened to "ture" after the opening verses.]

1. Let us sing of the King, the Supreme Brahman (Parbrahm) - the one incomparable God. ||1||
2. Whom Hari (Vishnu), Har (Shiva) and Brahma repeat in prayer - whose qualities have no limit. ||2||
3. As a tiny insect cannot grasp the orb of the sun - ||3||
4. so gods and demons too do not comprehend You; You alone are the knowing one. ||4||
5. He fills the body and the whole cosmos - from Him come the many living beings. ||5||
6. Again and again all things arise from Him - and perish at the end of the age. ||6||
7. Again the soul is dragged along by its karma (the fruit of its deeds) - fallen into the wildfire of delusion. ||7||
8. It passes through the eighty-four lakh forms of birth - there is no end to the wombs it enters. ||8||
9. Grass, crops and grain are brought forth - by the meeting of the rain-cloud and the earth. ||9||
10. Yet the crop never knew the cloud [that made it] - for the crop is without consciousness. ||10||
11. By this illustration it has been shown - so how then should the soul know Him? ||11||
12. He who has found refuge in the Name abides [in Him] - and to such a one He makes Himself known. ||12||
13. Water creatures live long lives [in the water] - yet the creature does not know that secret. ||13||
14. He by whose word the ages move on - by whom this world spreads out. ||14||
15. He sends sap into every single leaf - behold the water at the root. ||15||
16. Many kinds of flowers and fruits are produced - see it, within hard wood. ||16||
17. It grazes on grass and gives milk, curds and ghee - it is You who appoint the cow to yield. ||17||
18. From a single drop the body is formed - [and in it] man and woman sport in passion. ||18||
19. The guardians of the worlds and the five great elements - You sustain them all, unbroken. ||19||
20. Countless ages come into being in this way - mighty is Your word. ||20||
21. Thus we know You as nirgun (without attributes) - there is none above You. ||21||
22. Giving purpose to what is insentient - by You every work is brought to its end. ||22||
23. We see only by the light of the sun - yet the ignorant man says, "I see." ||23||
24. Though he has eyes he has become blind - for without the sun there is only darkness. ||24||
25. By this truth all things have their being - beyond all qualities, You are pure Being. ||25||
26. He breaks and fashions crores of universes - He grants their powers to Hari, Har and Brahma. ||26||
27. As His mind conceives, so it comes to be - the whole expanse of the universe out of nothing. ||27||
28. O mighty One, what is Yours and what belongs to Your own - that reckoning You alone know. ||28||
29. We know You as beyond understanding and beyond conceiving - the soul's refuge is Your Name. ||29||
30. In my ignorance I have offended You - in mercy, grant me rest. ||30||
31. By Your own will You lift [me] up - take me, let Your Name cling to me. ||31||
32. Through simple, guileless bhakti (devotion) He was met face to face - the beginningless Supreme Brahman. ||32||
33. Without Your will none can see You - not Sanak and the other sages and yogis, not even in a dream. ||33||
34. Knowledge, radiance and supreme bliss [are his] - who serves his own Supreme Brahman. ||34||
35. The wind moves within a fragrance - [then] leaves the scent behind and keeps its own nature. ||35||
36. So Hari moves within the qualities [yet stays untouched by them] - attributeless One, I repeat Your Name. ||36||

[Thus ends Shri Brahmaruli, complete ||3||]
